ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must complete the University of California (UC) Application. As a freshman applicant, you must complete a minimum of 15 year-long high school courses (A-G requirements) with a grade of C or better, including at least 11 finished prior to your last year of high school. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) is required. Selection for the Samueli School of Engineering is based on academic achievement in high school, with a strong emphasis on a record in mathematics and science. Applicants are required to answer four out of eight Personal Insight Questions. UCLA will not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes.
Description: The aerospace engineering program is designed for students interested in the design and development of aircraft and spacecraft. It is a four-year program that provides a broad and fundamental education in the engineering sciences and their application to the design and development of aeronautical and astronautical systems. The curriculum is based on a core of mathematics, physics, and chemistry, followed by a series of engineering science and design courses. Students are prepared for careers in the aerospace industry, in government, and in graduate study. The program is designed to provide students with the ability to apply knowledge of mathematics, science, and engineering; to design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data; to design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints such as economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability, and sustainability; and to function on multidisciplinary teams.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).
Accredidation: The Aerospace Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Description: The African American Studies Department offers a multidisciplinary curriculum that provides students with a broad understanding of the African American experience. The major is intended to provide students with a broad-based education in the humanities and social sciences, while also offering opportunities for more specialized study in specific areas of interest.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with German

For California residents, a minimum GPA of 3.0 is required, while nonresidents must have a minimum GPA of 3.4. Admission is based on a holistic review of the applicant's academic achievements, personal insight questions, and extracurricular activities. UCLA is test-free and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes. Applicants to the College of Letters and Science are admitted to the college and do not need to provide any additional information beyond the standard UC application.
Concentration: German
Description: The Department of European Languages and Transcultural Studies offers a major in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with five different concentrations: French and Francophone Studies, German, Italian, Scandinavian, and Transcultural Studies. The department's curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the historical, social, and cultural contexts that have shaped European identities. Our programs are designed to help students develop high-level proficiency in a European language, as well as the critical thinking and analytical skills needed to succeed in a globalized world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://admission.ucla.edu/apply/majors

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with Italian
Requirements: ELTS 1, Italian 1-6 or equivalent.
Concentration: Italian Studies
Description: European Languages and Transcultural Studies (ELTS) is the result of a merger between the departments of French & Francophone Studies, Germanic Languages, Italian, and Scandinavian. ELTS students explore European cultures through an experimental, transdisciplinary lens. While focusing on a specific language (French, German, Italian, or Scandinavian), students are encouraged to seek out connections between their primary area of study and the rest of Europe and beyond. The curriculum for each concentration is designed around four pillars of study: Experimental Humanities, Medical Humanities, Environmental Humanities, and Urban Humanities.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://reslife.ucla.edu/major-blast/humanities

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Languages and Transcultural Studies with Scandinavian
Requirements: To be eligible for admission as a freshman, applicants must complete 15 year-long college-preparatory courses (A-G requirements) with a grade of C or better: 2 years of History, 4 years of English, 3 years of Mathematics, 2 years of Science, 2 years of Language other than English, 1 year of Visual and Performing Arts, and 1 year of College-preparatory Elective. Applicants must earn a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (3.4 for non-California residents) in these courses. Admission also requires completion of the University of California application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions.
Concentration: Scandinavian
Description: The Department of European Languages and Transcultural Studies (ELTS) brings together UCLA’s distinguished programs in French, Germanic, Italian, and Scandinavian languages, literatures, and cultures. This union allows for a reimagining of our fields within a shared transcultural framework that addresses the complex history and the current state of Europe and its diverse global impact. The ELTS curriculum explores the intersections of language, literature, culture, and society, with an emphasis on interdisciplinary and transcultural perspectives. Students engage with a wide range of texts and media, from medieval manuscripts to contemporary film, and develop critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills. The European Languages and Transcultural Studies major is a single major with four tracks: French and Francophone Studies, German Studies, Italian Studies, and Scandinavian. Students must select one of the tracks.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in European Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in European Studies, applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application. General requirements for admission to UCLA include completion of the 'A-G' secondary school course requirements, a minimum GPA of 3.0 for California residents (3.4 for non-residents), and completion of the Personal Insight Questions. The European Studies major requires students to complete specific lower-division preparation courses, including foreign language proficiency through the intermediate level (six quarters or equivalent).
Concentration: Humanities, Social Thought, or Europe in the World
Description: The European Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study Europe from a variety of perspectives. Students choose a concentration in one of three areas: (1) Social Thought, (2) Humanities, or (3) Europe in the World. Within each concentration, students are encouraged to pursue their own interests by choosing from a wide range of courses in different departments.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Television
Requirements: To apply for the Film and Television BA program, applicants must complete the University of California Undergraduate Application and the UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television Supplemental Application. Required supplemental materials include a Personal Statement (no more than 2 pages, double-spaced), Writing Samples (a one-page Creative Writing sample and a Critical Essay of no more than 3 pages), and a list of Life Experience/Special Achievement. Freshman applicants must also complete the Personal Insight Questions on the UC Application.
Department: UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television
Concentration: film production (directing or cinematography), screenwriting, animation or digital media
Description: The Department of Film, Television and Digital Media (FTVDM) is one of the most prestigious programs in the world. Our mission is to educate the next generation of storytellers, scholars and leaders in the field. Undergraduate students take a variety of courses that provide them with a well-rounded education in the history, theory and practice of film, television and digital media. In their first two years, students focus on general education and lower-division requirements. In their junior and senior years, they dive into the major, taking courses in film history, theory and production. Seniors concentrate on an area of specialization such as film production (directing or cinematography), screenwriting, animation or digital media.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.tft.ucla.edu/admissions/film-television-and-digital-media/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender Studies
Requirements: To enter the Gender Studies major, students must have an overall grade-point average of 2.0 or better and have completed Gender Studies 10 with a grade of C or better. Preparation for the major includes Gender Studies 10 and one course from Gender Studies 102 through 187. All applicants must complete the University of California (UC) application, which includes Personal Insight Questions and a review of academic history.
Department: UCLA College of Letters and Science
Description: The Gender Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that examines the construction of gender and its intersection with other social categories such as race, class, ethnicity, and sexuality. Students explore how gendered experiences are shaped by history, culture, and power structures. The program is designed to give students a multi-disciplinary and rigorous understanding of the ways that gender and other categories of identity shape our world. Students will learn how to analyze and critique the structures of power that produce inequality and to imagine and work towards more just and equitable societies. The Department of Gender Studies at UCLA is a premier site for the study of women, gender, and sexuality, offering a broad, interdisciplinary program that explores the social and cultural construction of gender and the relationship between gender and other systems of power and difference.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

Requirements: Applicants must meet UCLA's undergraduate admission requirements. Freshmen are evaluated based on academic achievement in 'A-G' secondary school courses, grade point average, and Personal Insight Questions. Transfer applicants are evaluated on the completion of 60 semester (90 quarter) units of transferable college credit, GPA, and completion of major preparation courses. Required major preparation for the Geography B.A. includes Geography 1, 2, 5; one course from 3, 4, or 6; one course from Statistics 10, 12, or 13; and three additional lower-division courses as specified by the department.
Description: Geography is a diverse discipline that explores the relationship between people and their environments, and the patterns and processes of human and physical landscapes. Our undergraduate program provides students with a strong foundation in physical and human geography, as well as the spatial analysis tools (GIS, remote sensing) needed to address global challenges such as climate change, urbanization, and social inequality. The geography major is designed to provide students with a broad background in the field, while also allowing them to specialize in areas of interest through elective coursework.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography/Environmental Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to UCLA, freshman applicants must complete a specific set of 15 college-preparatory courses (A-G courses) with at least a 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-residents). Applicants must submit the University of California Application, which includes the Personal Insight Questions. For the Geography/Environmental Studies major specifically, students are typically admitted as 'Pre-Geography/Environmental Studies' majors and must complete the necessary preparation courses, including Geography 1, 2, and 5, with a minimum grade of C in each course and a cumulative 2.0 GPA to be eligible for the full major.
Description: The Geography/Environmental Studies BA major is intended for students who wish to focus on environmental issues from a geographic perspective. It provides students with a strong background in the physical and social sciences and allows them to explore the complex relationships between humans and their environments. The major has the following learning outcomes: knowledge of geography and the environment as a field of study, including its history and subfields; ability to identify, explain, and evaluate the impacts of humans on the environment and of the environment on humans; application of research methods to analyze and interpret geographic and environmental data; use of geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and other tools to represent and analyze geographic information; and application of critical thinking and communication skills to evaluate and communicate geographic and environmental information and issues.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geology/Engineering Geology
Requirements: Admission to the Geology/Engineering Geology major at UCLA is based on the general University of California admission requirements. For freshmen, this includes the completion of 15 year-long 'A-G' subject area courses with at least a C or better, a competitive GPA, and completion of the Personal Insight Questions. For transfer students, admission is based on the completion of major preparation requirements, which include: one year of calculus (Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A), one year of general chemistry (Chemistry and Biochemistry 14A/14B or 20A/20B), and calculus-based physics (Physics 1A, 1B or Physics 5A, 5B, 5C).
Concentration: Engineering Geology
Description: The Geology major is designed for students who want to study the Earth, its history, its materials, and the processes that shape it. The degree is based on a solid foundation in the basic sciences (math, physics, and chemistry) and a set of core Earth science courses. Students also have the opportunity to take advanced courses in a variety of topics, including geophysics, geochemistry, hydrology, environmental geology, and more. There are three possible tracks in the major: Geology, Engineering Geology, and Paleontology. The Engineering Geology track is for students who want to apply geological principles to civil engineering and environmental problems. It provides a solid background for students who want to work in the geotechnical industry or for government agencies that deal with geologic hazards, water resources, or environmental protection.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Jazz Studies

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global Studies
Requirements: Admission to the Global Studies major is competitive and requires a supplemental application. Students must first be admitted to UCLA and typically enter as 'Pre-Global Studies' majors. To be eligible for the major, students must complete five preparatory courses: Global Studies 1, one course from the 'Culture and Society' list, one from 'Governance and Conflict', one from 'Markets, Economy and Society', and one statistics course. A minimum GPA of 3.25 in these preparatory courses is required. The application for the major includes a personal statement. Transfer students must complete specific preparatory course requirements prior to admission. UCLA is a test-free institution and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.

Description: The Global Studies Interdepartmental Program (IDP) offers a major for undergraduate students that provides a rigorous, interdisciplinary education on the processes of globalization. The curriculum is designed to give students a multifaceted understanding of the processes and impacts of globalization, focusing on the interplay of the local and the global across economic, political, social, and cultural dimensions. Students learn to think critically about complex issues such as global governance, culture and identity, development and inequality, and conflict and peace. The Global Studies major is a designated capstone major, requiring students to complete a year-long senior thesis project that explores a specific topic related to globalization.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Greek and Latin

Description: The Greek and Latin major is designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the two major classical languages and literatures. It is particularly intended for students who wish to pursue graduate work in classics. Students should: acquire a broad knowledge of the classical world and its literature; demonstrate a high level of proficiency in Greek and Latin; read and analyze primary texts in Greek and Latin; communicate effectively in writing.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Human Biology and Society
Requirements: To be eligible for admission to UCLA, applicants must complete the 'A-G' college-preparatory courses with a minimum 3.0 GPA (3.4 for non-residents). Students are initially admitted to the 'Pre-Human Biology and Society' major. To transition to the Human Biology and Society B.A. major, students must complete specific pre-major courses—Life Sciences 7A, 7B, and 7C; Chemistry 14A, 14B, and 14BL (or 20A, 20B, and 20L); Statistics 13; and Society and Genetics 5—with a grade of C or better and a minimum cumulative and pre-major GPA of 2.0. A formal application to the major, which includes a 1-2 page personal statement, is also required.
Description: The Human Biology and Society B.A. and B.S. majors provide a holistic and interdisciplinary approach to the study of the biological and social dimensions of human health, medicine, and technology. Students in these majors explore how genetics, physiology, and evolution interact with social, cultural, and political factors to shape human lives. The curriculum integrates coursework from the life sciences, social sciences, and humanities, encouraging students to think critically about complex global challenges such as health disparities, environmental justice, and the ethics of biotechnology. The Human Biology and Society major is a designated capstone major. Students are required to complete a senior project that may be an individual or group research-based project, or a community-based internship and research project. The capstone allows students to integrate their prior coursework, use their knowledge to address a real-world problem, and develop professional and research skills.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Biology and Society
Requirements: Admission to the Human Biology and Society B.S. program is competitive. Freshman applicants apply to the 'Human Biology and Society (Pre-major)' via the University of California (UC) application. General admission requirements include completion of the 15 'A-G' college-preparatory courses with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (3.4 for non-residents) and completion of the UC Personal Insight Questions. Transfer applicants must complete specific major preparation courses prior to admission, which include a year of general chemistry, organic chemistry, life sciences (evolution, genetics, and molecular biology), and calculus. UCLA is a test-free institution and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes.
Department: College of Letters and Science (Institute for Society and Genetics)
Description: The Human Biology and Society major provides a holistic approach to the study of the human condition, emphasizing the bridge between the life sciences and the humanities and social sciences. Students are trained in the fundamentals of genomics and medicine, and in the history, philosophy, and sociology of science and medicine. The program aims to prepare students for careers in medicine, public health, law, public policy, and many other fields. The major provides students with a rigorous interdisciplinary education that prepares them to address some of the most pressing issues of the 21st century by examining how human biology, health, and disease are shaped by social, historical, and cultural factors, and conversely, how scientific research and technology impact society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Individual Field of Concentration
Requirements: To apply for the Individual Field of Concentration major, students must have a cumulative grade-point average of 3.3 (B+) or better and have completed at least 45 units, but no more than 120 units. The application process requires a written proposal that includes a statement of the objectives and nature of the proposed major, a rationale for why these objectives cannot be met by any existing UCLA major, and a list of specific courses to be taken. The proposal must be supported and signed by two faculty members, at least one of whom must be from the UCLA College of Letters and Science.
Description: The Individual Field of Concentration major is intended for students who have a clear, well-defined academic goal that cannot be met by any of the existing majors in the College of Letters and Science. It is not a shortcut to a degree, but rather an opportunity for highly motivated students to create a unique and rigorous program of study. To be eligible to propose an individual major, students must have a grade-point average of 3.3 (B+) or better and have completed at least 45 but no more than 135 units. The proposed major must be comprised of at least 48 upper-division units and be supported by a faculty sponsor.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) is [ucla.edu](https://www.ucla.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Individual Field of Concentration

The proposal must include a proposed major title, a summary of the theme and objectives of the major (about 50 words), a Statement of Purpose (limit 1500 words), and a detailed program of study consisting of 12 to 15 upper-division courses (at least 48 but no more than 60 units).
Description: The Individual Field of Concentration major is designed for students who wish to pursue a course of study that is not provided by any of the regular departmental or interdepartmental majors. The major must be comprised of at least 12 upper-division courses (48 units) and must be unified by a clear thematic focus. Each student is required to submit a written proposal for the major, including a description of the field of study and the specific courses to be taken, and must obtain the sponsorship of a UCLA faculty member who agrees to serve as the major advisor. The proposal must be approved by the College Faculty Executive Committee.

Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. It is a diverse field that includes the study of the structure of language (syntax, phonology, and morphology), the study of meaning (semantics and pragmatics), and the study of how language is used in context. Linguists also study how languages change over time, how they are learned by children and adults, and how they are processed in the brain. The Linguistics major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the core areas of theoretical linguistics: phonetics, phonology, syntax, and semantics. Students also take elective courses in other areas of linguistics, such as psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics, historical linguistics, and language acquisition.

The curriculum is divided into six fields: political theory, international relations, comparative politics, American politics, methods and models, and race, ethnicity, and politics.

Description: The Public Affairs major is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students to understand and address complex societal problems through a lens of social justice and equity. Students develop skills in analytical social science, including research design and data analysis, and learn how to apply these tools to address issues such as poverty, inequality, and environmental sustainability. A hallmark of the program is the year-long senior experiential learning project where students work in teams to apply their knowledge and skills to a real-world challenge in partnership with a community organization or government agency in the Los Angeles region.

The curriculum is designed to prepare students for diverse careers in public health or for further graduate study in the field. The program also offers opportunities for hands-on experience through internships and research projects, allowing students to apply their knowledge in real-world settings. With its focus on health equity and social justice, the BAPH program at UCLA Fielding is dedicated to preparing the next generation of public health leaders who will work towards creating a healthier and more just world.
